articles.title: US approves H-1B petitions without $100K fee
articles.summary: The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has started approving H-1B visa petitions that were filed without the $100,000 fee, following federal court orders blocking its enforcement, even as several applications remained pending beyond the 15-business-day deadline for premium processing.The approvals are a relief for employers who filed petitions in reliance on the court orders, though the pace of processing remains uneven, according to immigration law firm Meltzer Hellrung.Also Read: US proposes ending deference policy for H-1B extensions; Indian workers may face closer scrutinyThe development could also reopen hiring opportunities for employers who had avoided candidates based outside the US because of the fee.Federal courts blocked the feeThe $100,000 payment was introduced through a presidential proclamation in September 2025 and primarily affected certain new H-1B petitions for workers outside the US. The proclamation was extended on September 18, 2026, until September 21, 2027.Also Read: US ends 540-day automatic work permit extension for immigrants: What changes nowTwo federal courts have since blocked the fee. The US District Court for the District of Massachusetts vacated it in June 2026, with the First Circuit Court of Appeals subsequently denying the government's request to stay the ruling pending an appeal.In a separate case, the US District Court for the Northern District of California barred enforcement of the fee in late September, including under the extended proclamation. The government has appealed that ruling to the Ninth Circuit.USCIS has said it is complying with the court orders but would collect the fee if the orders are lifted. Both legal challenges remain pending.Delayed petitions begin movingEmployers had filed petitions without paying the fee, relying on the court rulings. However, many applications remained pending across USCIS service centres beyond the 15-business-day period applicable to premium processing.Meltzer Hellrung said it had organised a multi-company mandamus action to compel USCIS to adjudicate the delayed petitions. The firm said the approvals began coming through after it publicised the issue, without the lawsuit being filed.However, not all applications are progressing at the same pace. Petitions that remain pending beyond their premium processing deadlines may require further action, the firm said.Employers urged to reconsider overseas candidatesThe approvals could prompt employers to reconsider candidates based outside the US, many of whom had been screened out because their petitions were expected to attract the fee.Candidates who already hold a valid, unexpired H-1B visa stamp may be able to return to the US with a new employer's approved petition, potentially avoiding the need for a fresh consular visa appointment in many cases.Workers who have previously been counted against the H-1B cap and have time remaining under the six-year limit may also be eligible for a new petition without entering the lottery again.The firm said the overseas talent pool includes workers who left the US after layoffs or a lapse in immigration status, as well as those employed by multinational companies abroad.However, workers outside the US cannot begin employment under H-1B portability rules while awaiting approval. Employers may explore overseas contracting arrangements or employment through an employer of record, subject to applicable legal requirements.What employers should do nextEmployers are advised to review all pending petitions subject to the fee, particularly those filed under premium processing that have crossed the 15-business-day deadline without a decision.Also, employers whose petitions have been approved should promptly assess visa appointments and travel plans while the court orders remain in force. They should also reconsider candidates abroad who were previously excluded from hiring plans because of the fee.The firm recommended reviewing candidates' visa stamps, previous immigration status and H-1B histories before making offers, noting that individual circumstances will determine how quickly a worker can return to the US.

articles.title: 14 states agree to raise judicial officers' retirement age to 62 yrs: SC

The Supreme Court on Monday expressed satisfaction that as many as 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age of district judicial officers from 60 to 62 years and refused to list for urgent hearing the separate pleas of judges who are on the verge of retiring or have just retired.
"This pertains to the persuasive jurisdiction of this court. The issue is between the Supreme Court and the states," a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while declining to list individual pleas of judges who have to demit office after reaching the age of 60 years.
The CJI said that so far 14 states have agreed to raise the retirement age to 62 years and "we are hopeful that others will also follow." The bench said though it has listed the petition for hearing, it did not approve the moving of individual pleas by judicial officers.
Senior advocate Ranjit Kumar mentioned the plea for listing saying that judicial officers are retiring every day.

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: 5.7 lakh face evacuation risk
articles.summary: Cyclone Arnab is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Monday. The storm is expected to bring maximum sustained winds of 115-125 kmph, gusting to 140 kmph, prompting authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha to step up preparedness measures.Also read: Andhra on alert as depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into severe cyclonic stormAndhra Pradesh has identified around 5.7 lakh people as vulnerable to the cyclone, with evacuations scheduled to begin on Monday evening, a senior state disaster management official told Reuters. The state has also asked boats at sea to return to shore and directed officials to ensure the speedy restoration of power in case of disruptions.According to IMD’s Bhubaneswar unit, the deep depression over the eastcentral and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 15 kmph in the six hours leading up to 11.30 pm on October 25. It was centred near latitude 15.3°N and longitude 89.7°E, about 730 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 820 km from Kakinada and 990 km east of Bapatla.The weather agency said the system was likely to move northwestwards, intensify further and reach the westcentral Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of October 28. Winds are expected to strengthen as the system develops into a very severe cyclonic storm before making landfall by the forenoon of October 28.Also read: 'Very severe storm': IMD issues red alert in Odisha ahead of cyclone ArnabAndhra Pradesh, Odisha step up preparednessAndhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain on high alert and ensure preparedness across departments to minimise the cyclone’s impact.During a review meeting on Monday, Naidu instructed departments to coordinate closely and ensure that residents do not face difficulties due to the anticipated severe weather. He also directed district administrations to establish control rooms and provide timely guidance to the public.In Odisha, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the state government had reviewed the potential impact of Cyclone Arnab and assigned specific responsibilities to departments to ensure preparedness ahead of the system’s expected landfall. Schools and colleges in five districts will remain closed on Tuesday and Wednesday as a precautionary measure. The state government is also preparing to evacuate residents of low-lying areas to cyclone shelters.The government has also banned fishing and restricted tourist entry to hills, waterfalls, dams and other scenic destinations across six vulnerable districts, Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Koraput and Nabarangpur. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in these districts will remain closed on October 28 and 29. The state has deployed 24 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams and six National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, while eight ministers have been assigned to monitor preparedness. Authorities are shifting people from thatched houses and low-lying areas to shelters, moving pregnant women to health centres in advance and making special arrangements for senior citizens, children and persons with disabilities. Government employees’ leave in the affected districts has also been cancelled, and farmers have been advised to harvest and safely store crops that are 80-85% mature.Fishermen in Tamil Nadu stay ashoreIn Tamil Nadu, mechanised boat fishermen in Thoothukudi district stayed ashore on Monday after a cyclone warning was issued, avoiding fishing trips as a precautionary measure.Authorities in the coastal states are monitoring the developing weather system as it moves towards the eastern coastline.

articles.title: Trump names 2028 US election contenders
articles.summary: Michigan: US President Donald Trump, offering an early glimpse into the Republican Party's political future, named JD Vance and Marco Rubio among the prominent figures who could run for the White House in 2028, boasting that the GOP possesses a "great bench" compared to the Democrats.In an interview with FOX 2's Roop Raj ahead of Michigan rally, when asked directly about who might launch a presidential bid in 2028, Trump stated that while it is premature to name an outright front-runner, the party has no shortage of strong candidates."I could tell you who I think, but it's a little bit early," Trump said."We have great names - you have JD Vance, Marco Rubio, and many others. We have a great bench; they (Democrats) have no bench," Trump said.Earlier while leaving for Michigan rally, Trump while interacting with the media, also touched upon geopolitical and energy challenges stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war, reiterating that Washington would not allow global energy security to be compromised by the ongoing conflict."We're not going to be hostage with the oil industry over something that, frankly, should've never started," Trump asserted, reiterating his stance that the war was preventable.Meanwhile, the November 3 midterm elections are shaping up as a crucial contest for control of both chambers of Congress. The outcome will have significant implications for Trump's legislative agenda and the balance of political power in Washington.United States midterm elections are nationwide votes held every four years at the exact midpoint of a president's term. Acting as a major political temperature check for the country, these elections determine control of the federal government by putting all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and about one-third of the Senate up for grabs.The political contest comes amid broader challenges for the administration, including economic concerns and declining approval ratings. The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Trump's approval rating had fallen to 37 per cent in its polling, a low for a president heading into midterm elections in the publication's polling history dating back to 1990.
